proposal.hypothesis: A same-user BPR FM will provide complementary within-user ordering to the pointwise DeepFM branch, and adding it as an error-diverse portfolio member will increase trusted portfolio primary relative to 0.6061277485758569.
proposal.implementation_plan: Replace the delegated pointwise trainer with a visible k=16 categorical FM trained from Xs['train'][train_idx] and y['main'][train_idx]. In the train block, group selected rows by splits['train'].user_id, retain users having both long_view classes, and each epoch sample exactly one same-user negative for every positive. Score aligned positive and negative batches with shared FM parameters and minimize mean softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg)) using Adam at lr=0.001 with l2=0.0001 for 12 fixed epochs. Include a deterministic one-step sign assertion showing an update increases a synthetic positive-negative margin. Return the learned FM tensors; in predict, compute the same FM score over Xs[split] in bounded batches. No evaluation labels or checkpoint selection are used.
proposal.justification: The trusted metrics depend only on within-user order, so directly optimizing positive-negative margins within each user is aligned with the evaluation geometry. Replacing the pointwise DeepFM training objective with a shallow pairwise FM also creates a structurally different error pattern that may contribute even if its standalone score is lower.
proposal.observation: The supplied mechanism reports that vectorized same-user BPR improved an official FM from primary 0.601500738 to 0.603517127, while the active portfolio has substantial but imperfect diversity, including within-user rank correlation 0.8928231594133691 between w001 and w002 and 0.8327371603950816 between w002 and w003.

research_evidence.query: Which ranking objective and sampling implementation reliably improves the official FM?
research_evidence.reason: Cold-start runs repeatedly proposed BPR but implementation quality varied sharply.
research_evidence.summary: Use vectorized same-user BPR, not all-batch quadratic pairing. Build per-user positive blocks and negative pools only for users with both classes; use one sampled same-user negative per positive per epoch; align positive and negative arrays by user block; return safely when no eligible pairs; the FM global bias cancels. The exact loss is L=mean(softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg))). With diff=z_pos-z_neg, use g_pos=(sigmoid(diff)-1)/pair_count and g_neg=-g_pos. At diff=0, g_pos must equal -0.5/pair_count, never +0.5/pair_count; a one-step sanity check must increase z_pos-z_neg. At k=16, lr=0.001, one negative, the five-seed official-validation primary changed from 0.601500738 ± 0.000481897 for pointwise FM to 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR. Treat the mechanism and implementation invariants as the prior; rerun it inside the Agent harness rather than assuming the measured delta transfers exactly.

selection_rationale: Candidate 0 is the only viable candidate. It is a connected, falsifiable member-refinement experiment on parent w002: the DeepFM trainer demonstrably consumes target['engagement_aux'], and the patch replaces exactly one verified auxiliary target while holding architecture, auxiliary weight, optimizer, features, and prediction path fixed. Its dataset-specific train diagnostics support the hypothesis: is_hate is exceptionally sparse (rate 0.0004206) and essentially unrelated to long_view (phi -0.00394), whereas is_profile_enter is denser (rate 0.02539) and more positively related (phi 0.14613), making reduced negative transfer credible despite the correlation remaining weak. The uniqueness assertion, unchanged head shape, checksum change, and trainability check provide strong implementation reliability and clean attribution. It uses feedback labels only as train-only supervision, not inference features, and does not repeat the cited negative auxiliary-weight transition. Portfolio gain is uncertain because no residual-correlation diagnostic is supplied and prior target redesigns have elevated risk, but the candidate directly refines the active member and defines non-positive trusted marginal portfolio primary as falsification. With no competing viable candidate, it has the highest available expected reliability-weighted marginal portfolio value and information gain.
